question:
Priya plays netball with her friends during her school's Friday lunchtime session. She is also a member of her local netball club, where she plays in the regional league every weekend.
Compare Priya's experience of netball as recreation and her experience of netball as sport, and explain how these might impact on her performance.
markScheme:
Students are expected to answer in continuous prose, use good English, organise information clearly and use specialist vocabulary where appropriate.
AO1 - Knowledge of recreation and sport: recreation is usually fun, outcome is non-serious so winning is not important, flexible in organisation, modified rules, voluntary, self-officiated/regulated. Sport is highly organised and involves written rules; it is competitive so there is a winner; usually involves competitions with officials; commitment to regular training; extrinsic rewards; strategies and tactics.
AO2 - Application to Priya/netball: during the lunchtime session Priya is experiencing recreation; rules may be modified, such as shortened matches or reduced player numbers; played without umpires, with Priya and her opponents making decisions such as whether the ball landed in or out; she has chosen the activity in her free time during lunch; she is with friends so the activity is more likely to be fun and social; the outcome is not important to her. When Priya plays for her local club she is experiencing netball as sport; she is likely to train for games and play in competitions like the regional league; rules are codified and set by the NGB; there will be officials running her matches; her club may receive a trophy for winning the league.
AO3 - Analysis of impact on performance: because sport is serious, Priya will train more so the quality of her performance is likely to be better, eg her shooting will be executed with more accuracy and better technique; however, the serious nature of sport could lead to more deviancy when playing; with recreation, as the outcome is less serious, Priya may not put in as much effort, so quality may be lower, eg more passes going astray through a lack of concentration; playing netball recreationally could negatively impact her sport performance if poor habits develop; however, playing recreationally at lunchtime could help improve the skills she performs in league matches.
Accept any other appropriate analysis of Priya's experience of netball as recreation and sport.
Max 8 marks.

question: Identify three characteristics of physical recreation.
markScheme:
Award one mark for each of the following points.
- Physical recreation has modified rules (1)
- Physical recreation is usually self-officiated (1)
- Physical recreation is often done for intrinsic rewards/enjoyment/fun/stress relief/non-serious/health and fitness (1)
- Voluntary/choice/leisure time/not time bound (1)
Accept first three answers only. Accept other appropriate characteristics of physical recreation.
Max 3 marks.

question:
At a major international volleyball tournament, two pairs of players were charged with not using their best efforts to win a pool-stage match in order to secure a more favourable position in the knockout draw.
Discuss the extent to which the Olympic Oath is irrelevant at the modern Olympic Games.
markScheme:
Students are expected to answer in continuous prose, use good English, organise information clearly and use specialist vocabulary where appropriate.
AO1 - Knowledge of the Olympic Oath: a pledge read by one member of each country on behalf of all athletes; a compulsory element of Olympic participation; a traditional element introduced by Baron de Coubertin; first used at the 1920 Games.
AO2 - Application to the modern Games: the Oath is still read by athletes, coaches and officials at the opening ceremony of the summer and winter Games; the oath taker is from the host nation, holding a corner of the Olympic flag; the Oath has evolved to remain relevant, eg an oath for officials was introduced in 1972, and in 1999 the Oath was amended to reference doping/drugs after WADA was created; more recently the three oaths (athlete, coach, official) have been combined into one, recited by an athlete.
AO3 - Discussion of relevance: the Oath is still relevant as the underlying principles of the Games have not changed, being a celebration of sport and fair competition; cheats are still disqualified when caught, eg volleyball players tanking a match; athletes found to have doped have had medals stripped, showing the Games' ideals can still be upheld; audiences also uphold these ideals, showing disapproval of known drugs cheats.
The Oath could be seen as no longer relevant given greater media exposure increases the pressure to win and the temptation for deviant behaviour; lucrative sponsorship deals linked to winning may make the Oath less relevant; previously banned athletes are allowed to compete again once bans are served, raising doubts about a level playing field; allegations of state-sponsored doping programmes suggest pressure now comes from beyond the individual, undermining the Oath.
Accept any other relevant discursive point about the extent to which the Olympic Oath is irrelevant at the modern Olympic Games.
Max 8 marks.

question: Explain how the modern form of rugby union can match the concept of sport.
markScheme:
Students are expected to answer in continuous prose, use good English, organise information clearly and use specialist vocabulary where appropriate.
Rugby union has specific rules governing how it is played, which makes it highly structured, therefore matching the concept of sport.
- Highly structured - time/space/rules
- Rules externally enforced by officials
- Winning taken seriously/serious end product
- Skilful/refined skills
- Training/specialisation/trials/selective
- Administration - clubs/NGBs
- Display/spectators/entertainment
- Sophisticated facilities and equipment
- Pre-planned strategies/tactics
Accept other relevant explanations as to how the modern form of rugby union can match the concept of sport.
Max 6 marks.
